1.title: Introduction to Python
1.explanation: Python is a powerful programming language used to build software, websites, games, automation tools, data science applications, and artificial intelligence.
1.practice: Write a program that prints your name.
1.quiz: Which function displays text in Python?

2.title: Comments
2.explanation: Comments are notes that Python ignores. They help programmers explain their code.
2.code:
# This is a comment
print("Learning Python")
2.practice: Create a comment above a print statement.
2.quiz: Which symbol starts a single-line comment?

3.title: Variables
3.explanation: Variables store information so it can be used later in a program.
3.practice: Create variables named age and city.

4.title: Data Types
4.explanation: Python supports strings, integers, floats, booleans, lists, tuples, dictionaries, and more.
4.practice: Create one variable of each basic data type.
4.quiz: Which data type stores True or False?

5.title: Printing Output
5.explanation: The print() function displays information on the screen.

6.title: User Input
6.explanation: The input() function allows users to type information.
6.practice: Ask the user for their age.

7.title: Arithmetic Operators
7.explanation: Python can add, subtract, multiply, divide, and perform many other calculations.
7.code:
a = 10
b = 5
print(a+b)
print(a-b)
print(a*b)
print(a/b)
7.practice: Calculate the area of a rectangle.

8.title: Strings
8.explanation: Strings store text inside quotation marks.
8.practice: Store your favourite anime in a variable.

9.title: Lists
9.explanation: Lists store multiple values in a single variable.
9.practice: Create a list containing five numbers.

10.title: If Statements
10.explanation: If statements allow programs to make decisions.
10.practice: Create a program that checks if a number is positive.
10.quiz: Which keyword begins a decision statement?

11.title: Else Statements
11.explanation: The else statement runs when the if condition is false.
11.practice: Write a program that checks if someone can vote.
11.quiz: When does the else block run?

12.title: Elif Statements
12.explanation: The elif statement allows multiple conditions to be checked.

13.title: Comparison Operators
13.explanation: Comparison operators compare two values and return True or False.

14.title: Logical Operators
14.code:
age = 20
citizen = True
print(age >= 18 and citizen)
14.practice: Use and, or, and not in a program.
14.quiz: Which operator returns True only if both conditions are true?

15.title: For Loops
15.explanation: For loops repeat code over a sequence.
15.quiz: Which keyword starts a for loop?

16.title: While Loops
16.explanation: While loops repeat as long as a condition remains true.
16.quiz: When does a while loop stop?

17.title: Break Statement
17.explanation: The break statement immediately exits a loop.
17.practice: Stop a loop when the value reaches 7.

18.title: Continue Statement
18.explanation: The continue statement skips the current loop iteration.

19.title: Functions
19.explanation: Functions group reusable code into a single block.

20.title: Function Parameters
20.explanation: Parameters allow functions to receive data.
20.practice: Create a function that accepts an age parameter.
20.quiz: What are the variables inside a function definition called?

21.title: Return Statement
21.explanation: The return statement sends a value back from a function.
21.practice: Create a function that returns the square of a number.
21.quiz: Which keyword sends a value back from a function?

22.title: Scope
22.explanation: Variables created inside a function are local. Variables outside are global.
22.practice: Create both a global and a local variable.
22.quiz: What is a variable created inside a function called?

23.title: Modules
23.explanation: Modules are Python files that contain reusable code.

24.title: Packages
24.explanation: Packages organize multiple Python modules into one directory.
24.practice: Import and use the random package.

25.title: Exception Handling
25.explanation: Exceptions prevent programs from crashing when errors occur.

26.title: Reading Files
26.explanation: Python can read text files stored on your computer.
26.quiz: Which mode opens a file for reading?

27.title: Writing Files
27.explanation: Python can create and write information into files.
27.practice: Write your name into a file.
27.quiz: Which mode writes to a file?

28.title: Classes
28.explanation: Classes are templates used to create objects.

29.title: Objects
29.explanation: Objects are instances created from classes.
29.code:
class Robot:
    pass

r = Robot()
print(type(r))
29.practice: Create an object from your Car class.

30.title: Constructors
30.explanation: The __init__ method initializes object data when an object is created.
30.practice: Create a constructor with an age parameter.
30.quiz: Which special method acts as a constructor?

31.title: Inheritance
31.explanation: Inheritance allows one class to reuse the features of another class.
31.practice: Create a Student class that inherits from Person.

32.title: Polymorphism
32.explanation: Polymorphism allows different objects to use the same method name in different ways.
32.practice: Create two classes with the same method name.

33.title: Encapsulation
33.explanation: Encapsulation protects an object's data by keeping it inside the class.
33.practice: Create a class with a private variable.

34.title: Python Libraries
34.explanation: Libraries provide ready-made code that saves development time.

35.title: Installing Packages
35.explanation: Pip installs packages from the Python Package Index.

37.title: Lambda Functions
37.explanation: Lambda functions are short anonymous functions.
37.practice: Create a lambda that doubles a number.
37.quiz: What keyword creates a lambda function?

38.title: List Comprehensions
38.explanation: List comprehensions create lists using concise syntax.
38.code:
numbers = [x*x for x in range(5)]
print(numbers)
38.practice: Create a list of even numbers.

39.title: Dictionaries
39.explanation: Dictionaries store data as key-value pairs.

40.title: Tuples
40.explanation: Tuples are ordered collections that cannot be changed after creation.
40.practice: Create a tuple containing five values.
40.quiz: Can tuples be modified after they are created?

41.title: Sets
41.explanation: Sets store unique values and automatically remove duplicates.
41.practice: Create a set of your favorite numbers.
41.quiz: Can a set contain duplicate values?

42.title: JSON
42.explanation: JSON is a common format for storing and exchanging structured data.

43.title: Working with APIs
43.explanation: APIs allow Python programs to communicate with other applications and web services.

44.title: SQLite Databases
44.explanation: SQLite stores information inside a local database file.

45.title: Flask Basics
45.explanation: Flask is a lightweight Python framework for building websites and APIs.
45.code:
from flask import Flask
app = Flask(__name__)

46.title: Automation
46.explanation: Python can automate repetitive computer tasks.
46.practice: Think of one task you could automate.

47.title: Artificial Intelligence
47.explanation: Python is one of the most popular languages for artificial intelligence and machine learning.
47.quiz: Name one AI library for Python.

48.title: Building Projects
48.explanation: Projects combine everything you've learned into real applications.
48.practice: Plan a calculator, game, or website.

49.title: Python Best Practices
49.explanation: Writing clean, readable code makes programs easier to maintain.
49.practice: Rename unclear variables to meaningful names.

50.title: Congratulations
50.explanation: You have completed the Nitron Academy Python course. Continue practicing by building your own applications.
50.code: print("Congratulations! You completed Nitron Academy Python.")
50.output: Congratulations! You completed Nitron Academy Python.
50.practice: Build your own Python project from scratch.
50.quiz: What is the best way to improve your Python skills?
